The biggest bonus got the worst results.
Everyone says pay more, get more. The data disagrees.
In 2002, eighty-seven people in a town in rural India played six simple games.
A top score paid four rupees, forty, or four hundred.
Four hundred was close to a month's spending per person there.
Small or medium bonus: top score in about a quarter of the games.
At MIT, big pay helped plain key-pressing, but hurt adding up numbers.
When a task needs thinking, too much pressure backfires.
That's why the biggest bonus got the worst results.
